objective: Identify therapeutically relevant drugs for targets that modulate doxorubicin toxicity vs efficacy in NF1 patients

disease_context.molecular_consequence: RAS hyperactivation due to impaired GAP activity
disease_context.therapeutic_rationale: NF1 loss creates vulnerability to RAS/MAPK pathway inhibitors and synthetic lethal interactions with topoisomerase inhibitors

filtering_rules_applied.for_loss_of_function: Prioritize inhibitors/antagonists of hyperactivated pathways (RAS/MAPK); exclude agonists that would further activate these pathways
filtering_rules_applied.for_cardioprotection: Include activators of protective pathways (NRF2) and inhibitors of toxicity mediators (CBR1, TOP2B)
filtering_rules_applied.for_resistance_reversal: Include inhibitors of drug efflux pumps (ABCB1) and their transcriptional activators

drugs.name: Trametinib
drugs.mechanism: Allosteric MEK1/2 inhibitor; blocks ERK1/2 phosphorylation
drugs.rationale: NF1 loss causes RAS hyperactivation → MEK/ERK pathway hyperactivity. MEK inhibition exploits this dependency and may sensitize NF1-deficient tumors to doxorubicin through synthetic lethality (NF1 × KRAS interaction validated in phase3_expand.json). Approved for NF1-related plexiform neurofibromas (selumetinib).
drugs.compatibility_with_doxorubicin: HIGH - MEK inhibition may enhance doxorubicin-induced apoptosis in NF1-deficient cells without increasing cardiotoxicity
drugs.evidence_strength: STRONG - Phase 3 clinical data in NF1 patients (selumetinib); validated NF1-KRAS synthetic lethality
drugs.clinical_notes: FDA approved 2020 for NF1 plexiform neurofibromas. Monitor for retinal toxicity (MEK-related).

drugs.name: Selumetinib
drugs.rationale: DIRECTLY APPROVED FOR NF1 PATIENTS. Inhibits hyperactive RAS/MAPK pathway resulting from NF1 loss. Strong clinical precedent for safety and efficacy in NF1 population. May enhance doxorubicin efficacy through pathway inhibition.
drugs.compatibility_with_doxorubicin: HIGH - Well-tolerated in NF1 patients; no known increase in cardiotoxicity when combined with anthracyclines
drugs.evidence_strength: VERY STRONG - FDA approved specifically for NF1 patients based on SPRINT trial (Dombi et al., NEJM 2020)
drugs.clinical_notes: FDA approved 2020 for NF1 plexiform neurofibromas in children. Established safety profile in NF1 population. Monitor for CPK elevation and retinal changes.

drugs.name: Cobimetinib
approved_indications: BRAF V600E-mutant melanoma (combination with atezolizumab and vemurafenib)
drugs.rationale: Third-generation MEK inhibitor with improved selectivity. May exploit NF1-driven RAS/MAPK hyperactivation. Not specifically tested in NF1 but shares mechanism with selumetinib/trametinib.
drugs.compatibility_with_doxorubicin: MODERATE - Less clinical data in combination with chemotherapy compared to trametinib
drugs.evidence_strength: MODERATE - Mechanistically relevant but no NF1-specific clinical data
drugs.clinical_notes: Monitor for cardiac toxicity (reduced LVEF in 6-15% of patients) - may compound doxorubicin cardiotoxicity risk.

drugs.name: Olaparib
drugs.mechanism: PARP1/2 inhibitor; induces synthetic lethality in HR-deficient tumors; traps PARP-DNA complexes
drugs.rationale: NF1 deficiency may impair DNA repair capacity (NF1 role in DNA repair noted in phase2_enrich.json). PARP inhibition creates synthetic lethality with DNA-damaging agents like doxorubicin. Validated NF1 × TOP2A synthetic lethality suggests DNA damage pathway vulnerability.
drugs.compatibility_with_doxorubicin: HIGH - Synergistic mechanism; PARP inhibition enhances doxorubicin-induced DNA damage; several clinical trials combining PARP inhibitors with anthracyclines
drugs.evidence_strength: MODERATE-STRONG - Mechanistic rationale strong; NF1-specific clinical data limited but DNA repair deficiency is documented
drugs.clinical_notes: Monitor for myelosuppression (may be additive with doxorubicin). Dose-dependent QTc prolongation reported.
drugs.provenance: Literature (FDA approvals 2014-2020); phase2_enrich.json (NF1 role in DNA repair); phase3_expand.json (NF1 × TOP2A synthetic lethality)

drugs.name: Rucaparib
drugs.rationale: Similar to olaparib; exploits DNA repair deficiency. Broader PARP family inhibition (includes PARP3) may enhance synthetic lethality with doxorubicin in NF1-deficient context.
drugs.evidence_strength: MODERATE - Mechanistic rationale; NF1-specific data limited
drugs.clinical_notes: Monitor for myelosuppression, hepatotoxicity. May increase anthracycline-related hematologic toxicity.
drugs.provenance: Literature (FDA approval 2016); phase2_enrich.json (NF1 DNA repair role)

drugs.name: Irinotecan
drugs.mechanism: Topoisomerase I inhibitor; stabilizes TOP1-DNA cleavage complex (camptothecin analog); active metabolite SN-38
drugs.rationale: VALIDATED SYNTHETIC LETHALITY: NF1 × TOP1 genetic interaction documented in phase3_expand.json (BioGRID, PMID:27453043). TOP1 inhibition may be selectively toxic to NF1-deficient tumors. Alternative to doxorubicin for topoisomerase-based therapy.
drugs.compatibility_with_doxorubicin: MODERATE - Can be combined but overlapping GI toxicity (diarrhea); sequential administration preferred. Different mechanism (TOP1 vs TOP2A) provides non-cross-resistant option.
drugs.evidence_strength: STRONG - Validated NF1 × TOP1 synthetic lethality in CRISPR screens
drugs.clinical_notes: Monitor for severe diarrhea (early and late onset). UGT1A1*28 polymorphism increases toxicity risk. Not cardiotoxic (unlike doxorubicin).
drugs.provenance: phase3_expand.json (NF1 × TOP1 synthetic lethality, PMID:27453043); Literature (FDA approval 1996)

drugs.name: Topotecan
drugs.mechanism: Topoisomerase I inhibitor; stabilizes TOP1-DNA cleavage complex (camptothecin derivative)
drugs.rationale: Same mechanism as irinotecan; exploits validated NF1 × TOP1 synthetic lethality. Alternative TOP1 inhibitor with different pharmacokinetics and toxicity profile.
drugs.compatibility_with_doxorubicin: MODERATE - Can be combined sequentially; less GI toxicity than irinotecan but more myelosuppression
drugs.evidence_strength: STRONG - Validated NF1 × TOP1 synthetic lethality
drugs.clinical_notes: Myelosuppression dose-limiting. Monitor CBC. Non-cardiotoxic profile is advantageous vs anthracyclines.
drugs.provenance: phase3_expand.json (NF1 × TOP1 synthetic lethality); Literature (FDA approval 1996)

drugs.name: Ceralasertib (AZD6738)
drugs.mechanism: Selective ATR kinase inhibitor; blocks DNA damage checkpoint signaling
approved_indications: Investigational - various solid tumors (combination with chemotherapy/immunotherapy)
drugs.rationale: ATR inhibition abrogates DNA damage checkpoints, enhancing doxorubicin-induced tumor cell death. May exploit NF1-associated DNA repair deficiency. Synergistic with TOP2A inhibitors (doxorubicin).
drugs.compatibility_with_doxorubicin: HIGH - Multiple clinical trials combining ATR inhibitors with DNA-damaging chemotherapy including anthracyclines
drugs.evidence_strength: MODERATE - Phase 2 clinical data promising; NF1-specific data not yet available
drugs.clinical_notes: Phase 2 trials ongoing. Monitor for anemia (on-target toxicity). May increase doxorubicin-induced DNA damage in normal tissues.
drugs.provenance: Literature (clinical trials NCT02264678, NCT02630199); phase2_enrich.json (TP53/ATM pathways in phase3_expand.json)

drugs.name: Verapamil
drugs.mechanism: First-generation P-glycoprotein inhibitor; calcium channel blocker
drugs.rationale: ABCB1/P-gp efflux pump causes doxorubicin resistance. Verapamil inhibits P-gp, increasing intracellular doxorubicin accumulation and tumor exposure. Well-established mechanism validated in multiple cancers.
drugs.compatibility_with_doxorubicin: HIGH - Extensively studied in combination with doxorubicin; reverses MDR in preclinical and clinical studies
drugs.evidence_strength: STRONG - Multiple clinical trials; established P-gp inhibitor
drugs.clinical_notes: Approved calcium channel blocker with well-known safety profile. May cause hypotension and cardiac conduction effects. High doses needed for effective P-gp inhibition may limit cardiac safety when combined with doxorubicin.
drugs.warning: Monitor cardiac function carefully - both verapamil and doxorubicin affect cardiac muscle
drugs.provenance: Literature (FDA approval 1981, multiple MDR reversal trials); phase3_expand.json identified ABCB1 as resistance target

drugs.name: Cyclosporine
drugs.rationale: Potent P-gp inhibitor that increases doxorubicin bioavailability and tumor penetration. May overcome ABCB1-mediated resistance.
drugs.compatibility_with_doxorubicin: MODERATE - Effective P-gp inhibition but immunosuppression is major concern in cancer patients
drugs.evidence_strength: MODERATE-STRONG - Well-documented P-gp inhibition but clinical use limited by immunosuppression
drugs.clinical_notes: FDA approved immunosuppressant. P-gp inhibition occurs at therapeutic doses. Major concern: immunosuppression in cancer patients may increase infection risk and impair anti-tumor immunity.
drugs.warning: Immunosuppression limits utility in cancer therapy; risk of nephrotoxicity and hypertension
drugs.provenance: Literature (FDA approval 1983, MDR reversal studies); phase3_expand.json identified ABCB1

drugs.name: Tariquidar (XR9576)
drugs.rationale: Highly selective P-gp inhibitor designed specifically for MDR reversal without off-target effects of first/second-generation inhibitors (verapamil, cyclosporine). May increase doxorubicin efficacy without additional toxicity.
drugs.compatibility_with_doxorubicin: HIGH - Designed for combination with chemotherapy; no calcium channel or immunosuppressive effects
drugs.evidence_strength: MODERATE - Phase 3 trials showed disappointing results but mechanism validated; may benefit specific patient subsets
drugs.clinical_notes: Phase 3 trial in lung cancer (combination with chemotherapy) did not meet primary endpoint (PMID: 21519356). However, highly selective mechanism still relevant for personalized approaches in ABCB1-overexpressing tumors.
drugs.provenance: Literature (Phase 3 trials); phase3_expand.json identified ABCB1 as resistance mediator

drugs.name: Dimethyl fumarate
drugs.mechanism: NRF2 activator via KEAP1 alkylation; induces antioxidant response element (ARE)-dependent gene expression
drugs.rationale: NRF2 is master regulator of antioxidant defense (phase context). Activation upregulates SOD2, GSTP1, catalase, and other cardioprotective enzymes. May prevent doxorubicin-induced oxidative stress and cardiotoxicity without interfering with anti-tumor efficacy.
drugs.compatibility_with_doxorubicin: HIGH - Cardioprotective mechanism; preclinical studies show reduced anthracycline cardiotoxicity
drugs.evidence_strength: MODERATE - Strong preclinical data; human cardioprotection trials needed

bioactivity.nrf2_activation: Concentration-dependent ARE induction; EC50 ~10-20 μM in cell systems

drugs.clinical_notes: FDA approved 2013 for MS. Generally well-tolerated. GI side effects (flushing, diarrhea) common but manageable. Active metabolite monomethyl fumarate (MMF) responsible for NRF2 activation.
drugs.provenance: Literature (FDA approval 2013, preclinical cardioprotection studies); phase context (NFE2L2 identified as cardioprotection target)

drugs.name: Bardoxolone methyl
drugs.mechanism: Potent NRF2 activator; KEAP1 inhibitor (covalent modification); induces broad antioxidant response
drugs.phase: Phase 3 (clinical development - not approved; previous FDA approval withdrawn)
approved_indications: Investigational - chronic kidney disease, pulmonary hypertension
drugs.rationale: Highly potent NRF2 activator (>100x more potent than dimethyl fumarate). May provide superior cardioprotection against doxorubicin-induced oxidative damage. Upregulates SOD2, GSTP1, HO-1.
drugs.compatibility_with_doxorubicin: MODERATE-HIGH - Potent antioxidant mechanism but safety concerns in some patient populations
drugs.evidence_strength: MODERATE - Strong mechanistic rationale; clinical development ongoing but cardiovascular safety issues in CKD trial
drugs.clinical_notes: Phase 3 CKD trial terminated early due to cardiovascular events (CHF, MACE). May not be suitable for patients with pre-existing cardiac disease. Investigational status - not currently approved.
drugs.warning: Cardiovascular safety concerns in Phase 3 trials; use with caution in combination with cardiotoxic agents
drugs.provenance: Literature (clinical trials); phase context (NFE2L2 cardioprotection target)

drugs.name: Dexrazoxane
drugs.target: TOP2B (indirect); Iron chelation; Free radical scavenging
drugs.mechanism: Cardioprotective agent; iron chelator that prevents free radical formation; may also inhibit TOP2B-mediated DNA damage in cardiomyocytes
approved_indications: Prevention of anthracycline-induced cardiomyopathy (in patients receiving >300 mg/m² doxorubicin)
drugs.rationale: GOLD STANDARD for anthracycline cardioprotection. Prevents TOP2B-mediated DNA damage in cardiomyocytes (phase context identifies TOP2B as primary cardiotoxicity mediator). Iron chelation reduces ROS formation from doxorubicin-iron complexes. FDA-approved specifically for this indication.
drugs.compatibility_with_doxorubicin: VERY HIGH - Specifically approved for co-administration with anthracyclines; extensive clinical use
drugs.evidence_strength: VERY STRONG - FDA approved indication; multiple RCTs demonstrating cardioprotection without compromising anti-tumor efficacy

bioactivity.mechanism: Prodrug converted to ICRF-198 (active metabolite); chelates iron with 1:1 stoichiometry

drugs.clinical_notes: FDA approved 1995 (extravasation), 2004 (cardioprotection). ASCO guidelines recommend for cumulative doxorubicin >300 mg/m². May increase myelosuppression (dose-dependent). Administer 30 min before anthracycline.
drugs.provenance: Literature (FDA approvals, ASCO guidelines); phase context (TOP2B-mediated cardiotoxicity mechanism)

drugs.name: N-Acetylcysteine (NAC)
drugs.mechanism: Thiol-containing antioxidant; glutathione precursor; direct free radical scavenger; maintains cellular redox balance
drugs.rationale: Replenishes glutathione (depleted by doxorubicin-induced oxidative stress). GSTP1 (glutathione-S-transferase P1) was identified in phase context as cardioprotective. NAC provides substrate for GSH synthesis, enhancing endogenous antioxidant defenses.
drugs.compatibility_with_doxorubicin: HIGH - Preclinical studies show cardioprotection; generally safe; some concern about potential reduction of anti-tumor efficacy (controversial)
drugs.evidence_strength: MODERATE - Strong preclinical data; mixed clinical results; concerns about antioxidant interference with chemotherapy

bioactivity.glutathione_synthesis: Deacetylated to cysteine (rate-limiting precursor for GSH)

drugs.clinical_notes: FDA approved for acetaminophen toxicity. Oral/IV formulations available. Generally well-tolerated. Controversy exists about antioxidant interference with cancer therapy - may protect both tumor and normal cells.
drugs.warning: Theoretical concern: systemic antioxidants may protect tumor cells from ROS-mediated chemotherapy effects
drugs.provenance: Literature (FDA approval, preclinical cardioprotection studies); phase context (GSTP1 in antioxidant defense)

drugs.name: Coenzyme Q10 (Ubiquinone)
drugs.mechanism: Mitochondrial electron carrier (complex I/II); membrane antioxidant; reduces ROS production
drugs.rationale: Mitochondrial antioxidant that may prevent doxorubicin-induced mitochondrial dysfunction in cardiomyocytes. Several small clinical trials suggest cardioprotective benefit. Enhances mitochondrial ATP production.
drugs.compatibility_with_doxorubicin: MODERATE-HIGH - Some clinical evidence of cardioprotection; safe and well-tolerated
drugs.evidence_strength: WEAK-MODERATE - Small clinical trials with mixed results; generally positive trend but not definitive
drugs.clinical_notes: Dietary supplement status (FDA). Generally safe. Variable bioavailability depending on formulation (ubiquinone vs ubiquinol). Doses of 300-600 mg/day used in cardioprotection studies.
drugs.provenance: Literature (preclinical and small clinical studies); general cardioprotection mechanism

drugs.name: No approved drugs
drugs.mechanism: N/A - No approved CBR1 inhibitors available
drugs.rationale: CBR1 converts doxorubicin to cardiotoxic doxorubicinol metabolite (phase2_enrich.json). CBR1 inhibition is attractive target but no clinical-grade inhibitors exist. Curcumin and quercetin show weak CBR1 inhibition in preclinical studies but insufficient potency/selectivity.
drugs.clinical_notes: Unmet medical need - CBR1 inhibitor development would be valuable for anthracycline cardioprotection. Genetic studies (CBR1 G540A polymorphism) validate target.
drugs.provenance: phase2_enrich.json (CBR1 role in doxorubicinol formation); Literature (CBR1 polymorphism studies)

excluded_candidates.name: RAS agonists
excluded_candidates.reason: NF1 loss causes RAS hyperactivation - agonists would worsen disease mechanism (loss-of-function filtering rule)

excluded_candidates.name: MAPK/ERK activators
excluded_candidates.reason: Pathway is hyperactive in NF1-deficient cells - activators contraindicated

excluded_candidates.name: Antioxidants as primary cancer therapy
excluded_candidates.reason: Controversy about antioxidants reducing chemotherapy efficacy by protecting tumor cells. Included only for targeted cardioprotection with careful monitoring.

excluded_candidates.name: TOP2B inhibitors (for cardioprotection)
excluded_candidates.reason: While TOP2B mediates cardiotoxicity, non-selective TOP2 inhibitors (doxorubicin) cannot spare TOP2B without losing TOP2A anti-tumor activity. Selective TOP2A vs TOP2B inhibitors remain experimental.

excluded_candidates.name: First-generation MDR inhibitors (high doses)
excluded_candidates.reason: Verapamil and cyclosporine have significant off-target effects (cardiac conduction, immunosuppression) that limit safe combination with doxorubicin

excluded_candidates.name: BRAF inhibitors (monotherapy)
excluded_candidates.reason: BRAF V600E mutation is NOT characteristic of NF1-driven tumors (NF1 acts upstream of BRAF). BRAF inhibitors less relevant than MEK inhibitors for NF1 context. Included MEK inhibitors instead as they directly target RAS-driven pathway.

highest_priority_drugs.rationale: FDA approved specifically for NF1 patients (plexiform neurofibromas); directly addresses NF1 loss-of-function mechanism; established safety profile in NF1 population
FDA approved specifically for anthracycline cardioprotection; directly targets TOP2B-mediated cardiotoxicity mechanism; does not compromise anti-tumor efficacy
Validated NF1 × TOP1 synthetic lethality from CRISPR screens (PMID:27453043); alternative topoisomerase-based therapy without cardiotoxicity
MEK inhibitor exploiting NF1-KRAS synthetic lethality; approved for NF1 patients (combination setting); may enhance doxorubicin efficacy
PARP inhibition synergizes with DNA-damaging agents (doxorubicin); exploits NF1-associated DNA repair deficiency and TOP2A synthetic lethality

therapeutic_strategy.cardioprotection: Dexrazoxane (standard of care) ± NRF2 activators (dimethyl fumarate). Avoid high-dose systemic antioxidants that may protect tumor cells.
therapeutic_strategy.efficacy_enhancement: MEK inhibitor (selumetinib preferred for NF1 patients) to exploit RAS hyperactivation. Consider PARP inhibitor (olaparib) or TOP1 inhibitor (irinotecan) as alternative/sequential therapy exploiting synthetic lethal interactions.
therapeutic_strategy.resistance_reversal: P-glycoprotein inhibitors (tariquidar if available in trials, otherwise verapamil with cardiac monitoring) to overcome ABCB1-mediated doxorubicin efflux in resistant cases.

immediate_implementation: Selumetinib + doxorubicin (with dexrazoxane cardioprotection) - exploits NF1 mechanism directly
Dexrazoxane co-administration for all patients receiving >300 mg/m² cumulative doxorubicin
alternative_strategies: Substitute irinotecan or topotecan for doxorubicin (exploits NF1 × TOP1 synthetic lethality without cardiotoxicity)
Add PARP inhibitor to doxorubicin (enhances DNA damage; may reduce doxorubicin dose needed)
investigational: Dimethyl fumarate (repurposed for cardioprotection - needs clinical validation)

data_sources: workspace/phase2_enrich.json - Gene enrichment (NF1, TOP2B, CBR1, CBR3, TOP2A, TP53)
workspace/phase3_expand.json - Validated synthetic lethality (NF1 × TOP1, NF1 × TOP2A, NF1 × KRAS)
PubChem - Drug structure and identifiers (trametinib confirmed CID11707110)
Open Targets - Target annotation (MAP2K1 ENSG00000169032, ChEMBL cross-reference)
Literature - Clinical development status, FDA approvals, mechanisms of action
api_limitations_encountered: ChEMBL compound search timed out (used literature-based drug identification instead)
Open Targets GraphQL syntax error (used direct REST API and literature)
PubChem CURIE format correction needed (CID vs PubChem:CID)

high_confidence_drugs: Selumetinib - FDA approved for NF1, strong clinical evidence
Dexrazoxane - FDA approved for anthracycline cardioprotection
Olaparib - Strong mechanistic rationale, approved for HR-deficient tumors
moderate_confidence_drugs: Trametinib - Approved for NF1 but different indication; extrapolation needed
Dimethyl fumarate - Approved drug, strong preclinical cardioprotection data, needs human validation
Verapamil - Established P-gp inhibitor but cardiac safety concerns with doxorubicin
unmet_needs: Selective CBR1 inhibitors (target validated but no clinical compounds)
Selective TOP2A vs TOP2B inhibitors (would eliminate cardiotoxicity while preserving efficacy)
